common_name: Fan Scarlet Cardinal Flower (Compact Early-Blooming Seed Strain)

planting.note: Surface-sow seed (do not cover) indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost; Fan Scarlet is a compact, early-blooming seed strain of cardinal flower bred for uniform first-year flowering from seed.

directions: Plant in moist to wet, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun near water features, rain gardens, or boggy areas. Fan Scarlet was bred as a compact, uniform seed strain that reliably flowers the first year from seed and blooms earlier in the season than typical straight-species cardinal flower, producing the same brilliant scarlet flower spikes prized as the premier nectar source for ruby-throated hummingbirds, on a plant scaled for containers and smaller garden beds. Plants are short-lived perennials that self-seed freely; allow some seedlings to remain to perpetuate the colony, as individual plants typically live only two to three years.

common_name: Queen Victoria Cardinal Flower (Deep Burgundy Foliage with Scarlet Flowers)

planting.note: Surface-sow seed (do not cover) indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost; Queen Victoria bears deep burgundy-purple foliage that provides striking contrast with its brilliant scarlet flower spikes.

directions: Plant in moist to wet, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun near water features, rain gardens, or boggy areas. Queen Victoria bears deep, dramatic burgundy-purple foliage and stems that provide striking dark contrast beneath its brilliant scarlet flower spikes, standing out from the plain green foliage of the straight species and making a bolder statement in a border while still serving as the premier nectar source for ruby-throated hummingbirds. Plants are short-lived perennials that self-seed freely, though seedlings do not always come true to the dark foliage color; division of offsets in early fall helps maintain the true cultivar.
